wording: Supplier's total liability to Buyer under this agreement shall not exceed the total amount paid by Buyer in the 12 months preceding the claim, except for: (a) indemnification for IP infringement; (b) product liability for death or personal injury; (c) data breach or loss of confidential information. In no event shall either party be liable for consequential, incidental, or punitive damages.

Buyer owns all IP, including designs, improvements, know-how and derivative works created under this agreement. Supplier assigns all IP rights to Buyer upon creation. Supplier grants a royalty-free license to any pre-existing IP necessary to perform. Supplier warrants all deliverables do not infringe third-party IP.

Neither party shall be liable for failure to perform under this agreement due to events beyond its reasonable control (war, natural disaster, government action, port closures, shipping blockade). Performing party must: (a) suspension of performance is required, not termination; (b) notify other party within 48 hours; (c) resume performance within 30 days; (d) if suspension exceeds 90 days, either party may terminate without penalty. Force majeure does not include labour strikes, supplier's financial failure, or shipping delays.

Buyer commits to a minimum annual volume equal to 60% of the agreed forecast. Buyer may vary firm order quantities by +/-20% on 8 weeks' notice without penalty. Any shortfall below the flexibility band is payable at the agreed margin, capped at 10% of the committed value. Forecasts beyond the 8-week firm-order window are non-binding.

Supplier reserves the agreed weekly capacity (dedicated line) for Buyer and gives Buyer priority allocation in peak periods. Buyer pays a reservation fee of 3% of the committed value, credited against orders placed. Unused reserved capacity is released after 12 weeks' notice.

clause_name: Demand Reduction and Termination for Convenience
wording: Buyer may terminate for convenience on 90 days' written notice. Buyer pays for finished goods and for fabric and trims bought against firm orders; Supplier must mitigate by re-using materials and re-selling finished goods. No other liability arises from a reduction in demand.
Supplier shall not use forced, bonded, prison or compulsory labour or any form of human trafficking, and shall comply with the Buyer's Supplier Code of Conduct. Breach is grounds for termination.

clause_name: Supply Chain Due Diligence and Audit Rights
wording: Buyer may audit Supplier's factories on 14 days' notice. Supplier shall cooperate with audits and correct audit findings within the agreed corrective action period.

Where Supplier contributes to the development of Buyer products (co-development), all foreground IP, including improvements made by either party, vests in Buyer on creation. Supplier keeps its background IP and grants Buyer a perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use it with the products. Supplier shall not use Buyer-specific designs, patterns or tooling for any other customer, must keep a development log of its contributions and must flow these terms down to subcontractors. Know-how transfer materials are held in escrow. For 2 years after termination Supplier shall not make substantially similar products for a competitor of Buyer.
